title: Broncos Edge Seahawks 17-14 in Overtime Thriller on Thursday Night Football – NBC Sports
body:
Denver’s home crowd witnessed a dramatic finish on Thursday night as the Broncos edged the Seattle Seahawks 17‑14 in overtime, sealing the victory with a 53‑yard field goal from veteran kicker Wil Lutz. The decisive kick came just under five minutes into the extra period, following a pivotal interception by safety Ja’Quan McMillian that ended Sam Darnold’s late‑game drive. The win not only snapped Seattle’s momentum but also extended a quirky Broncos franchise streak: Denver has not surrendered a home game after leading by 11 points or more in the fourth quarter since a 2004 loss to the Raiders.

The game’s narrative was defined by its seesaw nature. Denver built a 14‑3 lead early in the second quarter, capitalizing on a balanced offensive attack that blended Russell Wilson’s poise at quarterback with a stout defensive front that forced three three‑and‑out series. The Broncos’ early advantage seemed secure until Seattle, led by Darnold’s poise under pressure, mounted a furious comeback in the final quarter. After a methodical drive that culminated in a 35‑yard field goal, the Seahawks narrowed the gap to 14‑10 with just over eight minutes remaining. A subsequent turnover forced Denver to punt, giving Seattle a short field and the opportunity to tie the game.

Seattle’s resurgence hinged on a series of aggressive play calls. Darnold, playing his first start of the season after a turbulent preseason, displayed a calmness rarely seen in a rookie. He orchestrated a 12‑play, 68‑yard march that featured a 22‑yard scramble and a tight‑end crossing route that set up the tying field goal. The Seahawks then forced a Denver three‑and‑out, recovered a fumble on the ensuing kickoff, and positioned themselves inside the Broncos’ 30‑yard line. However, a crucial sack by defensive end Dre’Drew Johnson forced Seattle into a fourth‑down attempt that fell short, preserving Denver’s lead heading into the final minutes.

The turning point arrived with just over two minutes left, when Darnold attempted a deep pass to wide receiver D.K. Metcalf that was read perfectly by McMillian. The safety’s interception halted Seattle’s final push and set up a short field for the Broncos. Rather than attempting to run out the clock, Denver’s coaching staff elected to play conservatively, forcing Seattle to use its remaining timeouts. After a series of short gains, the Broncos advanced to Seattle’s 38‑yard line, where Lutz, who has been reliable all season, lined up for a 53‑yard attempt. The kick sailed cleanly between the uprights, delivering Denver a 17‑14 win and preserving its long‑standing home‑field resilience.

Statistically, the Broncos’ defense posted a commendable performance, allowing just 260 total yards and forcing two turnovers, including the game‑changing pick. Offensively, Denver managed 210 yards, a modest total that underscored its reliance on timely big plays rather than sustained drives. Seattle, meanwhile, accumulated 285 yards and three first‑downs in the final quarter alone, illustrating the potency of Darnold’s late surge.

Looking ahead, the Broncos must build on this gritty victory as they prepare for a challenging road trip against the Kansas City Chiefs next week. Maintaining the defensive discipline that proved decisive against Seattle will be essential, especially against an offense that can exploit any lapse in coverage. For the Seahawks, the narrow loss serves as a learning experience for Darnold, whose poise in high‑pressure moments hints at a promising future. Both teams will likely adjust their strategies—Denver focusing on sustaining drives to avoid over‑reliance on field goals, and Seattle aiming to convert late‑game momentum into decisive scores. The overtime thriller not only provided an exhilarating finish for Thursday Night Football viewers but also set the stage for compelling storylines as the NFL season progresses.
